claim: Census completeness was recounted directly from the census state files for the Results section, rather than read out of a write-up, because the census is still running and the write-ups are snapshots.
status_note: Series recorded is the count of distinct series_instance_uid values per sop_class_name in _cache/census/records.jsonl, compared against the count of manifest rows per sop_class_name in _cache/census/manifest.csv. command:
python -c "import csv,json,collections;m=collections.Counter(r['sop_class_name'] for r in csv.DictReader(open('_cache/census/manifest.csv',newline='',encoding='utf-8')));s=collections.defaultdict(set);n=k=0
for line in open('_cache/census/records.jsonl',encoding='utf-8'):
    n+=1
    try: d=json.loads(line)
    except Exception: k+=1; continue
    s[d['sop_class_name']].add(d['series_instance_uid'])
print(n,k,[(c,m[c],len(s.get(c,()))) for c in m])"
notes: Supersedes nothing: F2-08 and F2-09 recorded the same quantities against an earlier snapshot of the same running census, 18,546 lines and RT Structure Set Storage at 9,183 series, and both remain correct as of their own snapshot. The RT Structure Set Storage figure had already moved to 18,439 of 19,358 by the time the guards were run against the finished draft, which is why results.md labels it a snapshot and why tests/test_results_doc.py recomputes completeness rather than asserting the count.
